definitions.explanation: causing laughter through humor or absurdity
so unreasonable or inappropriate as to be laughable

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{動|うご}きが{滑稽|こっけい}で{笑|わら}ってしまった。
examples.english: His movements were so funny that I couldn't help laughing.

examples.japanese: {滑稽|こっけい}な{話|はなし}を{聞|き}かせてくれた。
examples.english: He told me a funny story.

examples.japanese: そんな{言|い}い{訳|わけ}は{滑稽|こっけい}だ。
{自分|じぶん}の{失敗|しっぱい}を{滑稽|こっけい}に{話|はな}した。
examples.english: I talked about my failure in a humorous way.

examples.japanese: {必死|ひっし}になっている{姿|すがた}が{逆|ぎゃく}に{滑稽|こっけい}に{見|み}えた。
examples.english: The way he was desperately trying actually looked ridiculous.

examples.japanese: {滑稽|こっけい}な{顔|かお}をして{見|み}せた。

notes:
{滑稽|こっけい} describes something that causes laughter, either through humor or absurdity.

ETYMOLOGY:
- Originally from classical Chinese referring to jesters and entertainers
- In classical Japanese, used for comic storytelling

FORMS:
- Attributive: {滑稽|こっけい}な + noun
- Predicate: {滑稽|こっけい}だ/である
- Adverbial: {滑稽|こっけい}に

SENSE 1 VS SENSE 2:
- Sense 1: Positive - intentionally funny, entertaining
- Sense 2: Negative - unintentionally absurd, worthy of derision

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {滑稽|こっけい}な{話|はなし} (funny story)
- {滑稽|こっけい}な{姿|すがた} (comical appearance)
- {滑稽|こっけい}に{見|み}える (to look ridiculous)
- {滑稽|こっけい}さ (funniness, absurdity)

HISTORICAL NOTE:
- {滑稽|こっけい}{本|ぼん} refers to comic novels from the Edo period
- Example: {東海道中膝栗毛|とうかいどうちゅうひざくりげ}

SIMILAR WORDS:
- おかしい (funny - more casual)
- ばかばかしい (ridiculous - more negative)
- {面白|おもしろ}い (interesting/funny - more general)

REGISTER: Neutral to slightly formal. Literary flavor.
